behavior: Preserve bounded parallelism for independently authorized steps; existing policy has no global one-pending mandate. Native/public capture and external allocation atomically reserve potential failure capacity against current actual failed outcomes plus all unresolved same-task reservations, across steps, directories and restarts, under the existing common task reservation lock.

No new ledger, failure counter, mode marker or recovery authority. Derive native pending slots from existing safe reservation markers without matching validated terminal capture; derive external pending slots from existing unconsumed permits and allocated/admitted step counts, refusing contradictions/corrupt/partial unknown records. Actual failed counts remain actual observed failures, never relabel pending as failed.

Before creating native reservation, re-evaluate existing continuation policy using fresh task history while holding the common task lock; a terminal failure published between an earlier check and reservation cannot let a stale authorization exceed its ceiling. Release the lock before running the command; outstanding reservation continues to hold potential capacity.

Same-step retry requires its prior outcome; independently authorized other steps can run concurrently only while failed_count+pending_count is below the finite task failure ceiling. Also conservatively charge unknown pending outcomes against the existing three-signature allowance (max observed same-signature failures+pending_count<3), unless existing exact finite operator recovery applies. Do not trust changing labels to manufacture capacity.

Existing finite operator recovery preserves all histories and actual failed counts, changes only its already-authorized finite ceiling/signature policy, and cannot clear unresolved executions, override same-step pending, repair corrupt histories, or create an unbounded extension.

Terminal successful evidence releases pending capacity without increasing failures; terminal failure converts pending to one observed failure. Restart/unknown interruption retains its capacity until actual existing outcome reconciliation. Mixed native/external history continues to hold rather than merge counters or grant a fresh channel budget.

Default remaining potential failure capacity is the minimum of task allowance (6-actual_failed) and unresolved signature allowance (3-max observed signature count), with each pending reservation occupying one slot. Pending identities remain stable; no global serialization when at least two slots are available.

Actual seven-process distinct-step barrier cannot dispatch beyond reserved capacity or produce seven failures over default six. Positive controls prove at least two independent steps overlap when capacity exists; native stale-check race, same-step pending, terminal success release, non-Git/restart, external cross-step pending/ceiling and existing finite operator recovery remain enforced.
non_goals: No model/network/paid/live call, deployment or .nizam edit
No semantic signature classifier, guessed failure or new controller
No history conversion/reset or automatic unresolved evidence deletion
No global single-flight restriction when independent step capacity exists
unknown_outcome_boundary: Interrupted reservation without genuine terminal evidence remains a conservative reconciliation hold; no invented successful capture or operator consent.
